terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. Run your file here to add up the log, scrawled entries and all.

tasks.title: A number, or a fallback
tasks.description:
Under `# Task 1` in `log_totals.py`, write a function called `whole_number` that takes a text and a fallback. It gives back the whole number in the text, such as `3` for `"3"`, or the fallback when the text is not a whole number, such as `"two"` or `"2.5"`. Catch only the error that `int()` stops with for such a text. Any other error must reach the caller: given `None` instead of a text, `whole_number` stops with the error `int()` stops with. Print what it gives back for `"3"` and for `"two"`, with `0` as the fallback.

Check calls `whole_number` with texts and fallbacks of its own, and once with `None`, where the error must reach Check.
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson on try and except.
Try `int("two")` in a file of your own, and read the kind of error on the last line.
Put the line that turns the text into a number in a try, and name that error after except.
Give back the fallback from the except block.
hints: Run `int("two")` and `int(None)`: they stop with two different kinds of error, and only one of them is about text that is not a number.
`except ValueError:` catches only a `ValueError`. An `except:` with no name, or `except Exception:`, catches the `TypeError` for `None` too, and the task says that one must reach the caller.
The shape is `try:` with `return int(text)` moved in under it, then `except ValueError:` with `return fallback` moved in under it.

videos.title: Catching errors with try and except

tasks.title: One callout from the log
tasks.description:
Under `# Task 2`, write a function called `callout_of` that takes one entry of the log, such as `"Scarth Fell; 3"`, and gives back a tuple of its hill, without the spaces at its ends, and its hours as a whole number: `("Scarth Fell", 3)`. For hours that are not a whole number, such as `"Garve Edge; two"`, the hours are `None`: `("Garve Edge", None)`. An entry without exactly one semicolon is not a callout: it must stop with the `ValueError` Python gives when it takes the entry apart. Print what it gives back for `"Scarth Fell; 3"` and for `"Garve Edge; two"`.

Check calls `callout_of` with entries of its own, and with one that has no semicolon and one that has two, where the error must reach Check.
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson on catching only around the line that can fail.
Take the entry apart at the semicolon into two names, outside any try.
Turn the hours into a number inside a try, and use None when that fails.
Give back the tuple after the try.
hints: Two different lines can stop with `ValueError` here: the one that takes the entry apart, and the one that turns the hours into a number. Only one of them should be caught.
Put only the `int()` line inside the `try`. A `try` around the line that takes the entry apart catches its `ValueError` too, and the task says that one must reach the caller.
The shape is `hill, hours = entry.split(";")`, then `try:` with `number = int(hours)`, `except ValueError:` with `number = None`, and `return (hill.strip(), number)` after them.

tasks.title: Hours, and what could not be read
tasks.description:
Under `# Task 3`, write a function called `log_hours` that takes a list of entries and gives back a tuple of two things: the hours that can be read, added up, and a list with a text for each entry whose hours cannot be read, in order. Each text is the entry as it is, a colon, a space and the message of the error `int()` stopped with, such as `Garve Edge; two: invalid literal for int() with base 10: ' two'`. An entry without exactly one semicolon must stop with its `ValueError`, as in Task 2. Print what it gives back for `entries`.

Check calls `log_hours` with lists of its own, one where every entry can be read and one where none can, and one with an entry without a semicolon, where the error must reach Check.
nextSteps: Read the parts of the lesson on else and on what the caught error holds.
Start a total and an empty list before the loop.
In the loop, take the entry apart, then try to turn the hours into a number.
In the except, keep a text made from the entry and the error; in the else, add the hours.
hints: `except ValueError as error:` gives the caught error a name. An f-string with `{error}` in it shows the error's message, the words after `ValueError:` in a traceback.
The `else` of a `try` runs only when nothing in the `try` went wrong. Adding the hours there means an entry that could not be read never adds anything.
The shape is `except ValueError as error:` with `problems.append(f"{entry}: {error}")` under it, and `else:` with `total = total + number` under it.

tasks.title: A night's log, if there is one
tasks.description:
Under `# Task 4`, write a function called `night_text` that takes the path of a log file, as text, and gives back everything in the file as one text, or empty text when there is no file at that path. Open it with `encoding="utf-8"`; a `with` line closes it for you. Catch only the error for a file that is not there: any other error must reach the caller, such as the one for a path that is a folder. Print what it gives back for `"radio_log.txt"` and for `"tonight.txt"`.

Check makes files and folders of its own in a copy of your workspace, calls `night_text` for a file that is there, a path with no file, and a folder, where the error must reach Check.
nextSteps: Run your function for `"tonight.txt"` without a try, and read the kind of error.
Put the with block that opens and reads the file inside a try.
Name that error after except, and give back empty text there.
Try a folder too, such as `"."`, and see that its error still reaches you.
hints: The error for a missing file is the one the files issue showed: its name is on the last line of the traceback.
`except FileNotFoundError:` catches only a missing file. `except OSError:` catches every error of files and folders, the one for a folder among them, and the task says that one must reach the caller.
The shape is `try:` with the `with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as log:` block and `return log.read()` moved in under it, then `except FileNotFoundError:` with `return ""`.
